Question: Loki, Moe, Nick and Ott are good friends. Ott had no money, but the others did. Moe gave Ott one-fifth of his money, Loki gave Ott one-fourth of his money and Nick gave Ott one-third of his money. Each gave Ott the same amount of money. What fractional part of the group’s money does Ott now have?
Solution:
Because the three gifts are equal, use the common positive gift as one unit of money. Moe gave one-fifth of his money, so he originally had \(5\) such units. Similarly, Loki originally had \(4\) units and Nick had \(3\) units. Ott started with none, so the group's total was
\[
5+4+3=12\text{ units}.
\]
The gifts transfer money within the group, leaving this total unchanged. Ott now has the three gifted units, so his fraction of the group's money is
\[
\frac{3}{12}=\frac14,
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
